common_name: Garden Prince Almond (Self-Fertile Low-Chill Dwarf Almond)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter to early spring in full sun on well-drained soil, siting away from low frost pockets since bloom comes very early.

directions: Garden Prince is a genetic dwarf almond selected for a compact 6-9 foot habit and reliable self-fertility, so a single tree can set a full crop without a separate pollenizer, making it well suited to small home gardens or large containers. Its chilling requirement runs notably lower than standard almonds, which lets it break dormancy and bloom successfully in milder winter climates where many other almond cultivars fail to fruit well. Plant in full sun in deep, well-drained soil, since almonds suffer in wet or heavy ground, and protect the very early spring blossoms from late frost by avoiding low-lying planting sites. Harvest in late summer once the hulls split, then dry the nuts fully before storing.

common_name: Tonic Plantain (Ceres Tonic Forage Plantain Cover Crop)

planting.note: Broadcast or drill into a firm, weed-free seedbed in spring or late summer; Tonic establishes a deep-rooted, winter-active rosette that tolerates grazing and mowing.

directions: Tonic is a New Zealand-bred forage plantain cultivar selected for an erect, winter-active growth habit and high protein, mineral-rich foliage, and it has become one of the most widely used plantain cultivars in multi-species grazing and cover crop mixes. Its deep taproot draws up moisture and minerals from well below the topsoil, helping it stay productive through dry spells while also loosening compacted ground. Broadcast into a firm seedbed and roll lightly for good seed contact, then graze or mow periodically to keep the stand leafy and prevent it from bolting to seed. It is less cold-hardy than some newer plantain cultivars, so stands in colder zones may thin out faster over winter.

planting.note: Broadcast or drill into a firm, weed-free seedbed in spring or late summer as part of a grazing mix; allow several weeks of establishment growth before the first grazing or mowing.

directions: Ecotain is a purpose-bred environmental plantain cultivar developed in New Zealand specifically to reduce nitrogen leaching from grazed pasture, working through several modes of action including diluting urine nitrogen concentration from increased animal water intake and slowing the conversion of urine nitrogen into leachable nitrate. Beyond its environmental role, it functions as a productive, deep-rooted forage herb that tolerates drought and grazing similarly to other improved plantains. Drill or broadcast into a firm seedbed in spring or late summer, typically blended with grasses and clovers in a multi-species pasture or cover crop mix rather than sown as a monoculture. Graze or mow periodically to maintain leafy regrowth and keep the stand from running to seed.

common_name: Forage Feast Chicory (Palatable Grazing-Type Forage Chicory)

planting.note: Sow into a firm, weed-free seedbed in spring once soil has warmed; seed is small and should be covered only shallowly for even emergence.

directions: Forage Feast is a forage chicory cultivar that has performed well in grazing trials for its palatability to livestock, including notably strong preference shown by goats compared with other forage chicory types. Like other forage chicories it forms a deep taproot that scavenges nutrients and minerals from subsoil layers while the broad leaves suppress competing weeds and provide protein-rich grazing. It is somewhat less winter-hardy than some other forage chicory cultivars in cold climates, so stands may need to be managed as a shorter-lived component of a pasture or cover crop mix rather than relied on for many years of persistence. Mow or graze regularly to keep the rosette leafy and prevent bolting to seed.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach

planting.note: Sow into a firm, weed-free seedbed in spring or late summer; cover seed only shallowly since it needs light and even moisture to germinate well.

directions: Choice is a New Zealand-bred forage chicory selected from Grasslands Puna stock specifically to lower the levels of bitter sesquiterpene lactone compounds found in chicory foliage, reducing the risk of off-flavors tainting milk from grazing dairy animals. It grows in a more uniform, erect habit with smoother leaves than older chicory types and shows notably better winter-active growth, giving a longer grazing or cover window through cooler months. The deep taproot provides the same soil-opening and nutrient-scavenging benefits typical of forage chicory, while good leaf disease tolerance helps the stand stay productive. Graze or mow it regularly to encourage leafy regrowth and keep plants from bolting to seed.
sources: New Zealand Journal of Agricultural Research

common_name: Rosabrook Subterranean Clover (Red-Legged Earth Mite-Tolerant Self-Regenerating Clover)

planting.note: Sow in fall on well-drained, moderately acid soil for a self-reseeding winter annual cover; Rosabrook was bred to tolerate red-legged earth mite feeding better than older subterranean clover cultivars.

directions: Rosabrook is a subterranean clover cultivar developed as an improved replacement for the older cultivar Denmark, bred mainly for better cotyledon-stage tolerance to red-legged earth mite feeding damage during establishment. Like other subterranean clovers it buries its own seed pods at the soil surface after flowering, which protects the seed crop and gives the stand strong year-after-year self-reseeding without replanting. It suits well-drained, moderately acid soils and a mid-to-late-season growing window, forming a low, dense winter mat that suppresses weeds and fixes nitrogen for a following crop. The plant naturally dies back as temperatures rise in late spring, leaving buried seed ready to germinate again with the return of fall rains.
